# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 15 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_015_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 7

**1** "Why did she appear as an aged woman in the former visions, and now as a young woman?" **2** She answered: "Listen carefully. In the first two visions she appeared as an aged woman because your spirit was old and already withering, with no strength left on account of your weakness and wavering faith. **3** For just as the elderly who have no further hope of renewing their youth no longer look forward to anything except passing away — so you, worn out by the cares of this life, had given up on yourselves and were no longer being renewed by the Lord. But after he spoke to you through me, and you turned your hearts to him, you were renewed, your weakness fell away, strength returned to you, and you grew young. **4** And when you see the tower become a single stone, it will also happen in this way: all who have believed sincerely will be made into one — one body, one mind, one spirit, one faith, one love. When this occurs the tower will be completed, and all will rejoice together." **5** "I would also like to understand," I said, "why the stones from the deep sea are compatible with those from the dry land when they are placed in the building." **6** She replied, "Because they heard and believed. The sea-stones were tested and refined through fire, while the land-stones did not require such refinement."

---

*LOGOS note: "one body, one mind, one spirit, one faith, one love" — a pentadic unity formula echoing Ephesians 4:4-6 (one body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God).*
